title: Action → Skill Deliberate Practice
opening: Choose an action that serves a goal. You can explain an instruction and still miss the action when conditions change. Practice is useful when each attempt gives you something you can inspect and use.

labels.casePrompt: Compare how an area explanation changes across a repeated error, feedback and a new rectangle.
labels.workedExample: Worked example: explain why a rectangle's area changes
labels.gridLegend: Each tile is one square unit. A number marks a unit counted in this attempt; a blank tile remains in the rectangle but was left out.

cases.title: Same attempt, same error
cases.description: Repeat the same explanation five times: each attempt says a 3 by 5 rectangle has area 3 × 3 = 9. The error repeats because the explanation treats the rectangle like a square. The attempt count alone does not show improvement.
cases.worked: Each tile is one square unit. The mistaken count covers 9 tiles and leaves 6 out. A 3 by 5 rectangle has 15 square units.
cases.result: The error repeats. Keep the baseline visible, find a useful cue or condition to change, then try again.

cases.title: Feedback changes the next attempt
cases.description: Feedback points out that the sides can differ. Check the rule, then revise the same 3 by 5 example to use length times width: 3 × 5 = 15. This attempt changes in response to feedback.
cases.worked: Now all 15 tiles are included: length 3 × width 5 = 15 square units. Compare this changed attempt with the earlier 9-tile count.
cases.result: The next attempt changed after feedback. Compare its result with the baseline and record what still needs work.

cases.title: Test it in a new context
cases.description: Now explain a 4 by 6 rectangle. Calculating 4 × 6 = 24 applies the relationship to a new size. Repeating 3 × 5 = 15 would recall the earlier answer instead.
cases.worked: The new rectangle has 4 rows of 6 tiles: length 4 × width 6 = 24 square units.
cases.result: A different question tests use beyond the rehearsal. Record whether the action works there and what the conditions were.

feedback.unavailable: Saving is unavailable for this lesson. Your plan remains on screen.
feedback.missing: Complete the action, success criterion, baseline and practice plan before saving.
feedback.readFailure: Your saved practice could not be loaded. Your current plan remains here.
feedback.conflict: This practice changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here. Save again to keep these answers.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is still unresolved. Retry the same answers before changing them.
feedback.directAction: You can save a plan before you run the experiment.

practice.prediction: What goal will this action serve? Name the specific action, and what you will recognize as a successful attempt.
practice.observation: What is your baseline? Use a recent attempt, observation or result. If you do not have one yet, say what you will observe first.
practice.comparison: How will you prepare, carry out the action and reflect on each attempt? Which conditions should stay comparable?
practice.result: What result will you write down? What did you notice in your body, attention, thoughts or feelings while acting?
practice.revision: What improved? Which errors repeat? What part can you now perform without directing every detail?
practice.step: What will you change in the practice, and how will you test the action in the setting where you intend to use it?

source.status: The five source actions are preserved. Examples and interactive outcomes are illustrative teaching material, not observed learner outcomes or author-approved copy.
